boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented places for studying, recharging, recreation, and campus connection beyond a standard walkthrough.

cards.title: Sprague Library
cards.subtitle: Near Susan A. Cole Hall
cards.notes: Start on the main level for lending and research help, then use the posted floor maps to choose a quieter study area or a reservable room.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level library with study areas, media resources, and lending services.
cards.evidence_claim: The library tour identifies study areas on every level, group and collaborative rooms, and main-level laptop lending.
cards.access_notes: University Libraries states that Sprague Library is open to visitors; some services and reservable spaces have eligibility rules.

cards.title: Commuter Study Space
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library, first-floor south wing
cards.notes: Bring a charger and settle in near the Print and Laptop Lending Lab; use the large table or height-adjustable tables for an extended work session.
cards.short_summary: A bright library room with outlets, varied furniture, and a group table.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries page places the Commuter Study Space on Sprague Library’s first-floor south wing and lists outlets, a group table, and height-adjustable tables.
cards.access_notes: Listed as a drop-in study area during library operating hours.

cards.title: The Sensory Space
cards.subtitle: Room 030, Sprague Library Multimedia area
cards.notes: Reserve a two-hour session when a calmer setting would help; keep calls elsewhere, since Zoom calls are not permitted in this space.
cards.short_summary: A reservable, sensory-supportive retreat with privacy seating and comfort tools.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries page describes Room 030 as a dedicated sensory-supportive retreat and states that it can be booked for up to two hours.
cards.access_notes: Reservation required; the page says Zoom calls are not permitted.

cards.entity_name: Cole Hall Overlook Silent Study Space
cards.title: Cole Hall Overlook Silent Study
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library upper level, overlooking Cole Hall
cards.notes: Use this upper-level desk area when you need a quiet reading or writing block; choose it over group rooms when conversation is not part of the task.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent study area with a view toward Cole Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries study-spaces page identifies a large silent and quiet study area on the upper level overlooking Cole Hall.
cards.access_notes: Drop-in library study area during library operating hours.

cards.title: Creative Collaboration Pod
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library collaborative space
cards.notes: Reserve this pod for a project meeting that needs a shared screen and writable surface; arrive with your group’s files and a clear agenda.
cards.short_summary: A library pod designed for group assignments, media projects, and video conferencing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries page lists the Creative Collaboration Pod among spaces for group assignments, media projects, or video conferencing, with a monitor and whiteboard wall.
cards.access_notes: Reservable collaborative space for students, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Student Center
cards.subtitle: Campus hub for services, dining, and meeting space
cards.notes: Use the building directory to locate services, lounges, meeting rooms, or the cafeteria; it is a practical starting point before heading to a campus event.
cards.short_summary: A central building combining student services, dining, lounges, and program rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center’s official listing includes dining, student-service offices, lounges, ballrooms, meeting rooms, and outdoor spaces.
cards.access_notes: Check the Student Center for current building and event access details.

cards.title: Red Hawk Nest
cards.subtitle: Student Center Annex, Room 126
cards.notes: Meet classmates in this designated lounge before an activity or between classes; pair it with nearby Student Engagement and student-organization offices in the Annex.
cards.short_summary: A named Student Center Annex lounge close to student-engagement offices.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center’s official directory lists the Red Hawk Nest as lounge space in Room 126 of the Annex.
cards.access_notes: Located inside the Student Center Annex; observe building access rules.

cards.title: Commuter Commons
cards.subtitle: Student Center, third floor
cards.notes: Use the third-floor commons for a break or informal meetup, and take advantage of the adjacent lounge’s charging stations, TV, and seating.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor Student Center space alongside a lounge with charging stations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center directory lists Commuter Commons on the third floor and identifies an adjacent lounge with charging stations and TV.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Student Center; observe building access rules.

cards.title: Student Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Campus fitness, wellness, and recreation facility
cards.notes: Bring your valid university ID to use the gym, track, fitness areas, courts, lounges, or scheduled recreation programs; check the facility page for current operations.
cards.short_summary: A recreation facility with fitness space, courts, track, pool, lounges, and equipment lending.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s admissions page identifies the Student Recreation Center as the campus fitness, health, and wellness hub and lists its courts, fitness areas, track, pool, and lounges.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free to students with a valid Montclair State University ID.

cards.title: Student Recreation Center Pool
cards.subtitle: Student Recreation Center aquatics facility
cards.notes: Plan an open-swim visit with your university ID and follow the facility rules; no reservation is required for the posted general open-swim sessions.
cards.short_summary: A six-lane indoor pool offering general open swim.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation states that the pool offers general open swim without a reservation and requires a valid Montclair State University ID for facility entry.
cards.access_notes: General open swim is for students, faculty, staff, and alumni members; valid university ID required to enter the facility.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Sprague Library environments for quiet work, group projects, and media-focused study.

cards.title: Lower Level Silent Study
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library · Lower Level
cards.notes: Set up among the R–Z book area when you want a designated silent-study setting. Bring materials first, then choose an open desk booth.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level silent area beside the R–Z collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Sprague Library identifies an additional silent-study space on the Lower Level in the R–Z book area and shows desk booths there.
cards.access_notes: Drop-in silent-study space in Sprague Library; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Silent Study Overlooking Cole Hall
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library · Upper Level, south end
cards.notes: Use the upper-level overlook on the Cole Hall side for silent work. Pick a seat along the south end and keep calls for another area.
cards.short_summary: Silent seating with a view over Cole Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries describes large silent and quiet study spaces on the upper level overlooking Cole Hall at the south end.
cards.access_notes: Drop-in silent/quiet study area; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Silent Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library · Upper Level
cards.notes: Choose a carrel on the upper level for a contained individual-work setup. Keep your plan to quiet reading, drafting, or problem sets.
cards.short_summary: Upper-level individual carrels in a silent-study area.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries lists large upper-level silent and quiet study areas and documents Silent Study Carrels among its study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Drop-in silent/quiet study area; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Commuter Study Space
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library · First Floor, south wing
cards.notes: Head to the south-wing room for outlets, a large group table, and height-adjustable tables. It is near Print, Laptop Lending, and CAST.
cards.short_summary: A bright first-floor room with charging and adjustable tables.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries describes the Commuter Study Space as a first-floor south-wing room with outlets, a group table, and height-adjustable tables.
cards.access_notes: Drop-in space; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Room 201 Group Study
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library · Upper Level
cards.notes: Reserve Room 201 for an academic group session and use its table-and-monitor setup to share a screen while you work through material together.
cards.short_summary: A reservable upper-level room with a monitor.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries lists Room 201 as a Sprague Library group study room and documents it with a table, chairs, and monitor.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through University Libraries. Group rooms are intended for Montclair State students, faculty, and staff doing academic activities.

cards.title: Room 027 Collaborative Space
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library · Lower Level, Multimedia
cards.notes: Book this multimedia collaboration room when your project needs a shared display, whiteboard, or videoconference hardware. Plan an academic group task.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level collaborative room with display and whiteboard tools.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries states that Room 027 has a 65-inch Sony 4K TV, whiteboard, Polycom camera, and AirMedia controller.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through University Libraries; collaborative spaces are available to students, faculty, and staff for group assignments, media projects, or videoconferencing.

cards.title: Creative Collaboration Pod
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library · Collaborative Spaces
cards.notes: Reserve the pod for a compact team work session. Use the monitor, whiteboard walls, power outlets, and USB ports to keep a shared project moving.
cards.short_summary: A reservable pod with a monitor, whiteboard walls, and power.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries identifies the Creative Collaboration Pod as having a 55-inch monitor, whiteboard walls, power outlets, and USB ports.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through University Libraries; intended for academic group work, media projects, and videoconferencing.

cards.title: Group Study Pod #1
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library · First Floor
cards.notes: Reserve the first-floor pod for a small project meeting. Connect to its shared monitor, outline ideas on the whiteboard wall, and plug in devices.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor reservable pod for shared-screen coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries lists Group Study Pod #1 on the first floor and states that group study pods have a monitor, whiteboard walls, power, and USB ports.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through University Libraries; intended for academic group work, media projects, and videoconferencing.

cards.title: Viewing Room 001
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library · Viewing Rooms
cards.notes: Reserve this small viewing room for a focused media assignment or a compact group study session. Keep your group to the room’s one-to-four-person capacity.
cards.short_summary: A small reservable room for media viewing or group study.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries lists Room 001 among five viewing rooms for videotapes, DVDs, or group study, each sized for one to four students.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through University Libraries; viewing rooms are small and may be used by one to four students.

cards.title: The Sensory Space
cards.subtitle: Sprague Library · Room 030, Lower Level Multimedia
cards.notes: Reserve Room 030 when a calm, sensory-supportive study setting fits your work. Keep the visit within two hours and take Zoom calls elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: A reservable sensory-supportive retreat with privacy seating.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries describes Room 030 as a sensory-supportive retreat and states that it may be booked for a maximum of two hours; Zoom calls are not permitted.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through University Libraries for up to two hours. Zoom calls are not permitted inside; use a private study room for calls.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, photo-documentable destinations on Montclair-area corridors in the practical off-campus orbit of Montclair State University.

cards.title: Walk the reservation edge
cards.subtitle: Normal Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Start from the Normal Avenue side and use the county’s trail information to choose a walking route; Quarry Point is the documented scenic lookout.
cards.short_summary: A 157-acre county reservation with walking trails and a scenic overlook.
cards.evidence_claim: Essex County identifies Mills Reservation at Normal Avenue and Reservoir Drive and documents walking/jogging trails plus a cliff overlook toward the New York skyline.
cards.access_notes: The county lists the location as Normal Avenue and Reservoir Drive, Cedar Grove; trail conditions and access can vary.

cards.title: See the iris collection
cards.subtitle: Upper Mountain Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Plan around the garden’s listed 2026 hours and seasonal bloom cycle; the county says the main bloom is typically mid-May into early June.
cards.short_summary: A formal public garden with thousands of iris varieties on Upper Mountain Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Essex County documents more than 14,000 irises of about 3,000 varieties at Presby Memorial Iris Gardens, 474 Upper Mountain Avenue.
cards.source_title: Presby Memorial Iris Gardens | Essex County Parks
cards.access_notes: Listed 2026 garden hours are daily, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; confirm seasonal conditions before traveling.

cards.title: Use the paved pathways
cards.subtitle: Bellevue Avenue and North Mountain Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Enter from the Bellevue/North Mountain edge and follow the paved paths for a low-key walk; the county also lists the meadow for informal recreation.
cards.short_summary: An Upper Montclair county park with paved paths and an open meadow.
cards.evidence_claim: Essex County describes Anderson Park as a 14.85-acre park bordered by Bellevue and North Mountain avenues, with paved pathways and meadow space.
cards.access_notes: The county identifies the park boundary at Bellevue Avenue and North Mountain Avenue; use marked public entrances.

cards.title: Take a garden loop
cards.subtitle: Van Vleck Street corridor
cards.notes: Enter through the public gate and wander the six-acre garden grounds; keep amplified sound off and follow the foundation’s neighborhood-use guidance.
cards.short_summary: Admission-free public gardens on a residential Montclair street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Montclair Foundation states that Van Vleck House & Gardens at 21 Van Vleck Street has admission-free gardens open to the public daily from dawn to dusk.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | The Montclair Foundation
cards.access_notes: Gardens are open dawn to dusk, 365 days a year; the house is not open for public tours.

cards.title: Schedule a gallery visit
cards.subtitle: South Mountain Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition list, then book or purchase gallery entry before arriving; personal non-flash photography is permitted under the museum’s guidelines.
cards.short_summary: An art museum with changing exhibitions and studio-art programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair Art Museum lists its address as 3 South Mountain Avenue and documents gallery hours, exhibitions, and admission prices.
cards.source_title: Hours and Admission | Montclair Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours listed: Friday–Saturday 10 a.m.–6 p.m. and Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; tickets are available online or at reception.

cards.title: Set up a library stop
cards.subtitle: South Fullerton Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the Main Library’s posted desk hours for reading, research, or a librarian appointment; check the library calendar for any program-specific requirements.
cards.short_summary: Montclair’s main public-library location, with evening hours on weekdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair Public Library lists its Main Library at 50 South Fullerton Avenue and posts Monday–Thursday hours through 8 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Posted Main Library hours: Mon–Thu 10 a.m.–8 p.m., Fri–Sat 10 a.m.–6 p.m., Sun 1–6 p.m.; verify holiday closures.

cards.title: Choose a film screening
cards.subtitle: Bloomfield Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Review the current program and rating before buying; the cinema’s box office opens shortly before the first screening and closes after the last.
cards.short_summary: A six-screen nonprofit cinema for first-run, independent, documentary, classic, and foreign-language films.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair Film identifies The Clairidge at 486 Bloomfield Avenue as a six-screen cinema with year-round film screenings and special events.
cards.access_notes: The box office opens 15 minutes before the first daily screening and closes 15 minutes after the last; select films have accessibility services.

cards.title: Check the event calendar
cards.subtitle: Seymour Street corridor
cards.notes: Look up an all-ages-appropriate event before going, then use the theater’s directions from Bay Street or Walnut Street station to reach Seymour Street.
cards.short_summary: A Montclair performance venue one block off Bloomfield Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wellmont Theater lists its address as 5 Seymour Street and provides walking directions from the nearby Bay Street and Walnut Street rail stations.
cards.access_notes: Box office hours are listed as Monday–Friday noon–5 p.m., plus two hours before showtime on event days; event restrictions vary.

cards.title: Explore local-history resources
cards.subtitle: Orange Road corridor
cards.notes: Use the visit page to distinguish museum tours from the research library, and make an appointment before relying on the archives for a research stop.
cards.short_summary: A local-history organization with historic-house tours, gardens, and an archives library.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair History Center lists its office and library at 108 Orange Road and its Crane House & Historic YWCA museum at 110 Orange Road.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Montclair History Center
cards.access_notes: The office and library are listed Tuesday–Friday, 9 a.m.–3 p.m.; public museum tours occur on scheduled dates and gardens are open daily 8 a.m.–dusk.

cards.title: Browse the market stalls
cards.subtitle: Walnut Street corridor
cards.notes: Arrive within the posted Saturday market window and bring a reusable bag if shopping; vendors and seasonal offerings change, so consult the current lineup.
cards.short_summary: A Saturday market at the Walnut Street Train Station parking lot.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair Farmers’ Market states that it operates every Saturday at 86 Walnut Street, with seasonal hours and local farmers and food artisans.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Saturdays 8 a.m.–1 p.m. June–November and 9 a.m.–1 p.m. December–May; it operates rain or shine unless cancelled.
